thread:
Alex: Heads-up — hit an OOM in paged-attn running the 512B workload (seq=2048) under concurrency=16. Trace points to blocktable slab allocator failing to return blocks.
Rachel: ugh. which allocator are we talking about? slab per-size-class or a global buddy?
Alex: slab per-size-class (the fast path we enabled last week). Example log: `kernel: alloc_block slab(size=64)->NULL` then `panic: no free block`.
Samir: I noticed more fragmentation in blocktable heaps in the perf traces too. If typical requests allocate many small then a few large blocks, slab wastes a lot.
Kevin: can you attach a flame or paste eviction counters so we can see churn?
Alex: pasting the important counters from the soak run: slab_alloc_hits=4.8M, slab_free=3.9M, evicted_pages=120k, pager_faults=18k; p95 latency spiked during bursts.
Rachel: hypothesis: slab internal fragmentation -> increased pager churn -> KV page faults -> latency spikes and eventual OOM under sustained burst. Makes sense. :thinking_face:
Samir: Proposal: hybrid allocator. Keep slab for tiny fixed-size items (<=128B), use a region-based bump allocator for medium blocks backing paged KV entries, plus a per-worker LRU freelist for reuse. That should reduce fragmentation and keep fast paths.
Alex: rough sketch (pseudo):
```
// region bump allocator per thread/epoch
struct region { char *cur, *end; list freelist; }
alloc(size){
  if (size <= 128) return slab_alloc(size);
  if (region.cur + size <= region.end) { ret = region.cur; region.cur += size; return ret; }
  if (!freelist.empty()) return freelist.pop();
  // fallback to system/buddy for large allocations
  return sys_alloc(size);
}
```
Rachel: also add a compaction/coalesce path in the pager that merges adjacent freed blocks in the blocktable to get buddy-like behavior when fragmentation grows.
Kevin: nice. can we make compaction incremental so we don't get big pauses? maybe background per-shard compactor that does N bytes per tick.
Samir: ran a microbench on hybrid vs current-slab under concurrency=32:
- baseline (slab): p50=12.3ms, p95=48ms, peak-rss=2.1GB
- hybrid: p50=11.1ms, p95=34ms, peak-rss=1.72GB (mem -18%)
Compaction was configured incremental with 4KB work units; p99 slightly worse in one long-seq case.
Kevin: good numbers. Any regressions for very long sequences (seq=4096)?
Samir: seq=4096 stress: hybrid had +0.6% p99 due to occasional compaction pause; can be tuned by smaller increments. No OOMs in either.
Alex: next steps: prototype hybrid allocator + incremental compaction, add telemetry counters (alloc_type, frag_bytes, compaction_ms), and a canary flag `--kv-pager.alloc=hybrid` so we can do gradual rollout. @Kevin can you help add tracing hooks for blocktable alloc/free?
Kevin: yep, will add alloc_id tracing and an opt-in sampler to avoid noise. Also add event tags for page_fault vs eviction.
Rachel: let's run an e2e soak on Dedicated (reserve 4x burst) to validate cross-tenant noise and multi-tenant pressure. Add heatmaps for frag_bytes over time.
perf-bot: perf-run summary (candidate=hybrid vs main): throughput +3.2%, p95 latency -29%, peak-memory -18%, fragmentation -22%, OOMs 0->0. Artifacts: flamegraphs + alloc traces saved under s3://perf/artifacts/1802500000-hybrid-probe.
Alex: sweet. I'll open a draft PR with the allocator code + perf artifacts and link to this thread. Thanks everyone :rocket:
notes: thread discusses slab vs hybrid allocator for paged-attn blocktable, includes perf numbers and proposed implementation
